index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure illustrates the architecture of the AVAD (Audio-Visual Attention De-normalisation) layer, designed for spatially conditioned audio generation using visual guidance. The global layout is horizontally structured into two parallel processing streams: one for visual input and another for audio input, which converge at a central de-normalisation module. The top stream processes visual features, while the bottom stream handles audio features, culminating in a visual-guided de-normalisation step that refines the audio representation based on spatial relevance derived from the visual input.

In the visual stream, an image icon represents the input visual data, which is encoded into a 3D tensor denoted as u_{i,t}^v (a beige parallelepiped). This tensor passes through a Conv Layer (a rounded rectangle labeled 'Conv Layer'), producing a feature map (another beige parallelepiped). This feature map is then combined with positional embeddings via element-wise addition (indicated by a ⊕ symbol), followed by element-wise multiplication (⊗) with a relevance map. The relevance map is a grid of grayscale heatmaps (labeled 'Relevance Map') that captures the spatial influence of visual regions on the audio features. Two MLPs, labeled MLP_α and MLP_β, compute scalar modulation parameters α and β from this relevance map, which are used to guide the de-normalisation process.

The audio stream begins with an audio icon (a musical note with stars and waves) representing the input audio feature, encoded as a 3D tensor ũ_k^a (a blue-gray parallelepiped). This tensor is processed by a BatchNorm Layer (a rounded rectangle labeled 'BatchNorm Layer'), which normalises the features across the batch dimension. The output is then fed into a dashed-boxed module titled 'Visual Guided De-Normalisation'. Inside this module, the normalized audio features are first scaled by α (via ⊗) and then shifted by β (via ⊕), resulting in the refined audio feature ũ_{k+1}^a (a composite parallelepiped with gray and beige sections).

Connections between modules are indicated by arrows: the visual stream feeds into the relevance map computation, which in turn produces α and β via MLPs; these scalars are sent to the de-normalisation module. Additionally, a curved arrow connects the visual feature map after convolution to the de-normalisation module, indicating that the visual features themselves may also contribute to the modulation process. The overall design emphasizes that unlike prior batch-normalization-based approaches, AVAD performs de-normalisation guided by visual relevance, enabling precise spatial conditioning during audio decoding.
